text:
The federal court will likely deny the motion to remand and keep the case. The federal claims arise under federal law, so the court has original federal-question jurisdiction, and the plaintiff's own removal is not a bar to jurisdiction. The removal statute (§1441) lets only a defendant remove, so a plaintiff who filed in state court cannot remove, and the court will therefore grant the remand motion and send the case back to state court.

Correction: the first sentence above is wrong, and the last is right. The court will most likely **grant the motion to remand**, because only defendants may remove under 28 U.S.C. §1441(a), and the plaintiff-turned-remover has no removal right even though the case could have been filed originally in federal court.

CONFIDENCE: 95
